results.title: Big E opening day 2023 what you need to know
excerpts:
## What is the cost of admission?

The Big E offers a full season pass that you could purchase, which costs $70 for adults, and for children ages 6-12 costs $35. If you purchase tickets at the gate, it costs $20 for adults, $12 for children 6-12, and admission is free for children five and under.

  
There are some days during the fair that offers discounted tickets. Opening day is Be A Kid For A Day, which means that admission costs $12 for everyone. Military Appreciation Day is also opening day, and free admission is provided with a veteran or military ID to:

* Active duty and retired military personnel
* Dependents of active duty military personnel
* Veterans (no dependents)

There is also Eleven-After-Five, which means that tickets cost $11 after 5:00 p.m. Sunday through Thursday.

Senior Days are Sunday through Thursday and tickets will cost $16 for anyone 60 years old and over.

## How much does parking cost?

There is on-site parking that is available for $10 (cash only) in Lot 9.
Motorcycles can park in Lot 9 for $5 (cash only), and bicycles and bird scooters can park for free at 915 Memorial Avenue.

The Gate 9A area is available for drop-off/pick-up of passengers and has a large canvas tent with benches.

## Is there handicapped parking?

The Big E provides 580 handicapped accessible parking spaces on a first-come, first-served basis.

# How Much Does Big E Parking Cost?

Published on **September 29, 2025** | Written by [Alec Pow](https://www.thepricer.org/alec-pow/)  
This article was researched using 5 sources. See our [methodology](https://www.thepricer.org/methodology/) and [corrections policy](https://www.thepricer.org/corrections/) .

The Big E, officially the Eastern States Exposition, is one of the largest fairs in the United States and a major draw for New England residents each fall. Held in West Springfield, Massachusetts, the event attracts over a million visitors across its two-week run. With such huge crowds, one of the most pressing questions for attendees is how much parking will cost and what options are available. Parking costs can shape a family’s budget, influence arrival time, and even determine whether visitors drive or take a shuttle.
For many attendees, the parking fee is the first price they encounter before even stepping through the gates. Understanding the full range of fees helps avoid surprises at the lot and allows better planning for multi-day trips or larger vehicles. Below, we look at the different categories of parking at The Big E, real-world examples of costs, and the hidden fees that may impact the total.

## **Article Insights**

* Expert Insights & Tips

* Official Big E parking rates are **$10 (at $30 per hour, earning that amount would take about 20 minutes , before taxes) for cars** , **$5 for motorcycles** , and **$20 for campers or oversized vehicles** .
* Payment is primarily cash at Gate 9, though some off-site lots accept cards.
* Off-site parking with shuttles runs between **$5 and $15** , depending on location.
* Families driving from Boston or Hartford may face total transportation costs of **$45–70** including parking, gas, and tolls.
* Oversized vehicles may pay surcharges of **$10 or more** for extra space.
* Free bicycle parking and low-cost shuttles offer alternatives for locals.
* Arriving early, carpooling, or using transit are the best ways to save.

Big E Parking Cost

## **How Much Does Big E Parking Cost?**

Parking at The Big E is straightforward, but it comes with variations depending on the type of vehicle. As of 2024–2025, the official **Big E parking costs are** **$10 (about 20 minutes at $30 per hour) for cars and trucks** , **$5 for motorcycles** , and **$20 for campers or oversized vehicles** . The most common payment method remains cash at the gate, especially at the main entrance, Gate 9, though some off-site lots accept cards.
These prices have held steady for several seasons, though increased traffic and demand during peak days can make availability more valuable than the face price.

The Big E does not charge extra for admission parking privileges, but the traffic leading into the fairgrounds means the time cost can be significant. Visitors arriving late in the morning often face heavy congestion on Memorial Avenue, which is the main route into the lots. According to the Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT, 2023), traffic volumes around the fairgrounds peak between 9 a.m. and noon, leading to added delays and higher stress levels.

[EasternStatesExposition](https://www.easternstatesexposition.com/p/about/getting-here) notes that this public parking lot is the main accessible option for visitors, although it operates on a cash-only basis and tends to fill up quickly, especially on weekends.
Visitors are advised to arrive early, ideally before 10 AM, to secure a convenient parking spot and avoid long delays due to heavy traffic.

In addition to the [official parking lot](https://www.thebige.com/p/generalinfo/bigeinfo) , many local residents offer unofficial parking on their lawns near the fairgrounds, with prices varying from approximately **$5 to $30** based on proximity to the entrance. These spots usually accept cash only and provide a shorter walk compared to more distant parking areas. However, according to [Reddit discussions](https://www.reddit.com/r/prked/comments/1n0ndz6/parking_tips_for_the_big_e_at_the_eastern_states/) , in-season traffic and local road congestion can make arriving and leaving the event challenging during peak times.

Parking management during the event is supported by local law enforcement directing traffic to the quickest routes, often overriding GPS suggestions.
Visitors are cautioned to avoid street parking in nearby neighborhoods due to strict towing and ticketing enforcement. Weekday visits offer a less stressful parking experience, while weekends require more advance planning and patience.

* [How Much Does Disney Vacation Club Cost?](https://www.thepricer.org/how-much-does-disney-vacation-club-cost/ "How Much Does Disney Vacation Club Cost?")

## **Real-Life Cost Examples**

A family of four driving in from Hartford might arrive at 10 a.m. and pay **$10 (about 20 minutes at $30 per hour)** to park their sedan at Gate 9. With admission tickets, food, and rides, their total day could easily top **$250** , but the parking fee itself is a flat charge.
A solo motorcycle rider from Amherst pays **$5** to park in the designated motorcycle section, which is closer to the main entrance. This option often saves both money and walking distance, especially for repeat visitors who know the layout.

Also check our articles on the cost of [SeaWorld parking](https://www.thepricer.org/how-much-does-seaworld-parking-cost/) , [Six Flags parking](https://www.thepricer.org/how-much-does-six-flags-parking-cost/) , or parking lot striping.

For camper families, the fee can be higher. A couple from Worcester bringing a mid-size camper for a weekend stay paid **$20 per day** , plus an additional **$10** when their unit exceeded the allotted space. Over three days, their total came to **$90** just for parking, not including camping amenities.

Vendors face even steeper logistics. One produce seller with a large truck reported paying **$20 daily** for oversized parking in 2022, in addition to vendor-specific access permits.
Their weekly total reached over **$200** solely for parking, showing how costs scale with duration.

## **Cost Breakdown**

The pricing tiers at The Big E are relatively simple compared with other large state fairs. Here is a clear view of the rates:

|**Vehicle Type** |**Daily Parking Cost** |**Notes** |
| --- | --- | --- |
|Cars/Trucks |**$10** |Main lots, typically paid at Gate 9 |
|Motorcycles |**$5** |Designated motorcycle zones, closer to entrances |
|Campers/Oversized |**$20** |May incur an extra **$10** if space is exceeded |
|Bicycles |Free |Limited racks available near entrances |

This table reflects official 2024–2025 rates as published by The Eastern States Exposition office (Big E, 2024). Off-site private lots can range between **$5 and $15** depending on distance and whether shuttle service is included.

## **Factors Influencing the Cost**

Several variables determine how much visitors will actually pay.

...

These lots are operated by local businesses and residents looking to benefit from the influx of cars.

The Big E also supports a shuttle system from off-site parking areas, reducing the need for fairground entry congestion. Ride-share services like Uber and Lyft have designated drop-off zones near the gates, though surge pricing can spike fares during peak hours. Public transit remains an option, with the Pioneer Valley Transit Authority (PVTA) running buses to West Springfield during fair weeks at fares starting under **$2 per ride** .

## **Ways to Spend Less**

There are several strategies for cutting parking costs at The Big E. Carpooling remains the most effective way to lower the per-person cost. Four adults splitting the **$10** fee end up paying only **$2.50 each** , which is cheaper than public transit from most nearby towns. Motorcyclists also benefit from lower rates and easier access.

Arriving early often secures a closer spot, saving time and the need for a shuttle.

...

Longtime fairgoers also recommend downloading the Big E’s digital map in advance to know exactly where lots and gates are located, reducing confusion during heavy congestion.

## **Total Cost of Ownership**

Parking fees are just one part of the equation. A family driving from Boston, roughly 90 miles away, faces fuel costs of **$25–30** round trip, plus tolls on the Mass Pike that add another **$6** . Adding the **$10** parking fee brings their total travel cost near **$45** before even buying admission tickets. Over several days, this adds up quickly.

For regional visitors, especially those driving from other New England states like Connecticut or Vermont, the travel and parking bill can exceed **$70** for a single day. These totals show how transportation contributes to the full cost of attending The Big E, beyond just the gate ticket price.

WEST SPRINGFIELD, Mass. (WWLP) – The Big E Fair in West Springfield is right around the corner, and attendees are preparing to buy their tickets.
[LIST: Get ready for The Big E Fair’s 2025 food lineup](https://www.wwlp.com/news/local-news/the-big-e-fair/list-get-ready-for-the-big-e-fairs-2025-food-lineup/?ipid=promo-link-block1)

[The Big E Fair](https://www.thebige.com/p/generalinfo/bigeinfo) is the largest event on the East Coast and the fourth-largest fair in North America, but how much does it cost to get in?

## Admission Prices

The 2025 regular-price admission tickets are $20 for adults, $16 for seniors, and $12 for children ages 6 through 12, kids under 5 are free.

Presale tickets do offer a discount; however, all ticket sales are final. If you buy tickets in advance through September 10th, they are $17.50 for adults and $12 for children ages 6 through 12. If you plan to go to The Big E multiple times, there is a value pass option that gets you in daily during the 17 days of the fair for $71.50 per adult and $36.50 for children ages 6 through 12.

For $33.
50, you can also get one wristband that includes unlimited rides at the Midway on the day you visit, Monday through Friday, or 78 credits on Saturday or Sunday.

## How much does parking cost?

If you plan to park on the Big E fairgrounds, all main parking will be found at Gate 9, which is the first gate on Memorial Avenue if you are coming from the east (from Springfield, Route 5, I-91, etc.) and the last gate if coming from the west (Agawam). It is cash-only parking, and there are no ATMs near the gate, so you will have to have $10 on hand to park. Motorcycles can park for $5 at Gate 9.

## About The Big E Fair

The 17-day long fair features hours of free entertainment and attractions, terrific food, authentic New Orleans Mardi Gras in The Big Parade, an immersive Ireland adventure in the International Plaza’s Dingle Peninsula Showcase, North American Midway, as well as educational opportunities from the Avenue of States to Storrowton Village Museum, Farm-A-Rama, and more.

# Spend the day

Review of The Big E

Reviewed September 25, 2011

I have visited the fair over 40 times. In this review, let's start with parking. Don't pay more than $5 to park...you will be walking all day at the fair, so what is a few extra steps? Park down one of the side streets across from the main gate and you'll likely pay 3-5 instead of 10-20. Parking on the fair grounds is $10.  
50% of the fair is food and much of it is fried, including Oreos, PB &J and brownie bites.

...

Booking a hotel has to be done way in advance, especially over a weekend, or do as we do and stay around Hartford, CT, a little south of the fair, and visit Cabela's before you leave. Some cheaper hotels in that area.  
  
Parking can also get very crazy, we usually end up parking at one of the town businesses that advertises parking and walk from there.  
  
I highly recommend attending. Be sure to take a break and take in some of the entertainment, like the shows and circus. Besides, it gives your feet some time to rest!
